note: an unanswered case, its book kept

24.label: Beadle Bicker
24.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Steady: Working beside them, you do not tire.

52.label: Blood Court: Hal de Witt
52.desc: Hal de Witt stands before the Blood Court for Burglary at van der Meer's Pawnshop. The charge looked like full proof.

55.label: Petty Thief: Hodge Chandler
55.desc: Hodge Chandler, a rival in the trade. Walked from Fire at the Mercer Warehouse. Petty Thief, espieur. 1 crime on the record. Wears great hobnailed boots, a soldier's.

items.label: A lit taper dropped carefully
items.text: What the fire started with. Cheap, and handled.

result.label: The Hand on the Kindling
result.text: A clean thumb on the one part that did not burn.

suspects.name: Hodge Chandler

suspects.name: Neeltje Welser
suspects.motive: The clerk had been skimming from the books, and the books were in the counting-room.

suspects.name: Nan Gerber

56.label: Unanswered: Fire at the Mercer Warehouse
56.desc: The trail went cold. Hodge Chandler walked. With the Rolls, this can be opened again in Study.

ask.label: A locked door
ask.text: The back room is locked. Instinct finds the key under the sill; a watchman puts a shoulder to it. Left locked, whatever is behind it stays there.

ask.label: The light is going
ask.text: The window dims. Wit works on by candle; Instinct works by feel. Neither, and you strain your eyes into the night.

suspects.name: Hal de Witt

items.label: Marks on the Sill
items.text: The print of a hand on the whitewash. Faint, but there.

result.label: The Hand Read
result.text: Under vinegar and the red umbrella the hand comes up whole: a thumb with a scar across it. Good enough for the Court.

items.label: Blood on the Glass
items.text: They cut themselves going in, or out.

result.label: The Blood Read
result.text: A great deal of it. The barber-surgeon in the Abbey Close stitched a hand the same morning.

items.label: The Getaway
items.text: Wheel-ruts across the gutter, a cart with the tail-board up. They did not care who saw.

items.label: No Forced Entry
items.text: Not a mark on the locks. Whoever came in had a key, or was let in by someone who trusted them.

journal.title: The Trail Goes Cold
journal.text: Fire at the Mercer Warehouse goes into the Rolls unanswered. Somewhere in The Market, Hodge Chandler hears the crier and laughs.

journal.title: Taken: Hal de Witt
journal.text: The sergeants take them at their shop, in front of everyone. The charge is full proof. Now it is for the sworn men.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at the Mercer Warehouse. You find: The Smell Under the Smoke, The Message, A Hobnail Scar. The first name in the casebook: Nan Gerber.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Week 4
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 8 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Corroborated Account
journal.text: The body of the thing and the words of the witnesses finally agree. They point the same way. It was Hal de Witt, the owner's partner in trade. It has to be.

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with the Mercer Warehouse before anyone can tidy it. Whatever you find there next will be on record.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Matthes Bicker walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: The Confessor: Leave the seal alone
journal.text: He is grateful, and says so where the Bishop can hear it. (The Bishop's favour)

journal.title: The Confessor
journal.text: A priest of the parish asks for a word. Someone told him something under the seal, and it is eating him. He will not break the seal. He might point. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: A Reason
journal.text: A gentle question, then another. Hal de Witt is angry about something, and it comes out sideways. The partnership is drowning in debt, and a theft is a loss the guild will forgive.

journal.title: Hailed
journal.text: A woman runs up to you, out of breath, pointing. It is going to be a long day. The long way round, and your legs know it.

journal.title: Hue and Cry
journal.text: You are hailed in the street. Somebody set fire to the Mercer Warehouse while the family slept upstairs. It started with a lit taper dropped carefully. The message came the next morning: a list of other shops.

journal.title: Week 3
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 7 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over van der Meer's Pawnshop. You find: The Getaway. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Hodge Visscher. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: The round hears things: a word about Burglary at van der Meer's Pawnshop.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without the Vinegar and Umbrella, you only get part of it. Under vinegar and the red umbrella the hand comes up whole: a thumb with a scar across it. Good enough for the Court. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: A Purse on the Desk: Pocket it
journal.text: Silver is silver. Somebody now believes you can be bought, because you can. (+3 Coin; the Council's eye)

journal.title: A Purse on the Desk
journal.text: Nobody saw who left it. Three Coin, good silver, and a note with the name of a case on it and nothing else. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over van der Meer's Pawnshop. You find: Marks on the Sill, Blood on the Glass. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Bess Pietersz. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Matthes Bicker takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked.

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book: Buy the page
journal.text: A page in a bad hand, with a name on it that you were going to have to find the hard way. (A token that names a name)

journal.title: The Pawnbroker's Book
journal.text: A pawnbroker keeps a book of everything that came through his door this week, and who brought it. Something from your case is in it. He would part with the page. (The clock waits for your answer.)

journal.title: Week 2
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 5 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The blade was a chisel, chipped at one corner. Find the chisel, find the burglar. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: You spend six hours on your feet in the rain outside the bear-garden.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at van der Meer's Pawnshop. The back shutter has been forced with something flat and patient, and the strongbox stands open like a mouth. You come away with The Pried Shutter, The Inventory. A name for the casebook: Hal de Witt. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: Yourself Again
journal.text: A moment on the bench, and you are yourself again.

journal.title: Drawn
journal.text: You fill a sketch-book with van der Meer's Pawnshop before anyone can tidy it. Whatever you find there next will be on record.

journal.title: The Pattern
journal.text: You took the Council's letter because something in this city does not add up: too many small crimes that fit together too neatly. Nobody else sees it yet. The first case on the desk is a burglary. Start there.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at van der Meer's Pawnshop
journal.text: Splinters everywhere at Lijsbet Barker's. Someone went through the shop window, with a cobble during the storm, took the window display, and was gone before the watchman finished shouting. A neighbour reports seeing a cart with the tail-board up.
